delegation_propre.instructions: Do the methods carrying MCP annotations (@Tool, @ResourceTemplate, @Prompt) only call an injected service and format its result, without themselves loading data, parsing JSON, searching or filtering?

criteria.true: Every annotated method delegates the lookup to an injected service; loops, filtering and JSON parsing live in the non-annotated class
criteria.false: At least one annotated method loads the catalogue, parses JSON, or searches or filters the data itself

defaut_principal.instructions: Which of these is the most serious defect of this MCP server, if any?

criteria.none: No notable defect against the conventions
criteria.missing_primitive: A tool, resource template or prompt from the conventions is absent
criteria.poor_descriptions: Tool or argument descriptions too vague for an agent to use
criteria.logic_in_adapter: Business logic or data loading inside the MCP-annotated class
criteria.unhandled_errors: Not-found or invalid input cases are not handled

absence_geree.instructions: When the requested service name does not exist in the catalogue, do the annotated methods return a readable message to the caller instead of throwing an exception or returning null?

criteria.true: Each annotated method handles the not-found case with an explicit message
criteria.false: At least one annotated method throws, returns null, or ignores the not-found case

descriptions_utiles.instructions: How useful are the description strings of the @Tool and @ToolArg annotations to an AI agent that must decide which tool to call and how to fill its arguments?
criteria: Descriptions are missing, empty, or only repeat the method or parameter name
Descriptions say what the tool does, but not what the argument expects nor what the tool returns
Descriptions say what the tool does, what each argument expects (format or example), and what the tool returns
